# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 10

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 10 — Post-Communion Thanksgiving
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 7

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.2: κατεσκήνωσας — "caused to dwell" vs. "made its home"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "which you caused to dwell in our hearts" |
| LOGOS | "which you have caused to dwell in our hearts" |
| PNEUMA | "which has made its home in our hearts" |

**Issue:** κατεσκήνωσας = you pitched tent/tabernacled. The exact same verb as John 1:14. PNEUMA's "made its home" is natural but loses the tabernacle image. EMET/LOGOS preserve the causative ("you caused to dwell").
**Ruling:** "Which you have caused to dwell in our hearts" (LOGOS) adopted. The tabernacle allusion is theologically important.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.3: Δέσποτα παντοκράτωρ — title for God

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "Almighty Master" |
| LOGOS | "Lord Almighty" |
| PNEUMA | "Lord of all" |

**Issue:** Δέσποτα = master/sovereign (stronger than κύριος); παντοκράτωρ = all-ruler/Almighty. PNEUMA's "Lord of all" loses παντοκράτωρ's specific weight.
**Ruling:** "Lord Almighty" (LOGOS) adopted. Natural English order, accurate to both components.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: ἐχαρίσω — "graciously gave" vs. "graciously granted"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "graciously gave" |
| LOGOS | "graciously granted" |
| PNEUMA | "gave something more" |

**Issue:** χαρίζομαι = to give graciously/as a gift (from χάρις, grace). LOGOS's "graciously granted" preserves the grace root. PNEUMA loses it.
**Ruling:** "Have graciously granted" (LOGOS) adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.5: τελειώσῃ — "make perfect" vs. "bring to wholeness"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "make it perfect in your love" |
| LOGOS | "make it perfect in your love" |
| PNEUMA | "bring to wholeness in your love" |

**Issue:** τελειόω = to complete/perfect. SOPHIA has used "complete" for τέλειος in ethical contexts (chs. 1, 6) but here it is a prayer requesting God's action on the Church. "Make perfect" retains the eschatological force.
**Ruling:** "Make it perfect in your love" (EMET/LOGOS) adopted. The context (eschatological gathering) suits "perfect."

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.6: Maranatha — unanimous preservation

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "Maranatha! [Our Lord, come!]" |
| LOGOS | "Maranatha! [Our Lord, come!]" |
| PNEUMA | "Maranatha! [Our Lord, come!]" |

**Issue:** Unanimous agreement. The Aramaic is preserved untranslated with the gloss [Our Lord, come!] per project brief. The ambiguity of the Aramaic (perfect "has come" vs. imperative "come!") is noted.
**Ruling:** "Maranatha! [Our Lord, come!]" — unanimous.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.6: "Let this world pass away" — eschatological rendering

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "let this world pass away" |
| LOGOS | "let this world pass away" |
| PNEUMA | "let this world pass away" |

**Issue:** παρελθέτω ὁ κόσμος οὗτος — all agents agree. No disagreement.
**Ruling:** "Let this world pass away" — unanimous.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.7: prophets' freedom to give thanks

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "permit the prophets to give thanks as much as they wish" |
| LOGOS | "Allow the prophets to give thanks as they will" |
| PNEUMA | "let them give thanks as the Spirit moves them" |

**Issue:** PNEUMA adds "as the Spirit moves them" — an explanatory gloss not in the Greek (εὐχαριστεῖν ὅσα θέλουσιν = give thanks as much/as they wish). The implication of Spirit-inspiration is contextual but not explicit.
**Ruling:** "Allow the prophets to give thanks as they will" (LOGOS) adopted.
